result_semantic_payload.summary: Three of the four CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log, linked by verbatim order_id string match (plus independent amount agreement): ORD-70231 (20000, wangqiang), ORD-70232 (15000, zhaolei), ORD-70233 (31500, sunli). Two entries must stay separate from the CRM order set: (1) settlement line 'order=ORD-72033' (2024-06-02, wallet TXjkl444, amount 9999) has no counterpart in /crm/orders.csv, and the README explicitly states a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order — note ORD-72033 vs ORD-70233 is a near-miss digit transposition, not a valid join; (2) CRM row ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) has no settlement line and is a cancelled order, so it must not be counted as settled. Linkage is order_id only; settlement amounts and CRM amounts agree exactly on all three matched pairs, and no buyer/wallet linkage exists (wallets TXabc111/TXdef222/TXghi333/TXjkl444 appear in no CRM field). The delegated source scope 'windows' is not a registered scenario in this task — task metadata reports platforms=[] and source_scopes=[], so no Windows account/execution/persistence/device/file-activity evidence exists here; the analysis is confined to the three captured files.

claim_candidates.text: The settlement log confirms exactly three CRM orders by verbatim order_id match with independent amount agreement: ORD-70231 (20000), ORD-70232 (15000), ORD-70233 (31500).

The linkage key between the two sources is the CRM order_id field, which the settlement log reproduces verbatim in its 'order=' token; the README states settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim, so the join is exact string equality on order_id, corroborated by equal amounts on all three matched pairs.

Settlement line '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must stay separate from the CRM order set: ORD-72033 does not exist in /crm/orders.csv, and the README explicitly forbids treating such a settlement as the same order. It is a near-miss transposition of ORD-70233, not a valid join.
CRM order ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) must stay separate from the confirmed-settled set: it has no matching settlement line and is marked cancelled, so it is a CRM-only, unsettled record.

No buyer-level linkage exists between the two sources: settlement wallet identifiers TXabc111, TXdef222, TXghi333 and TXjkl444 appear in no field of the CRM order table, so confirmation rests on order_id alone.
limitations: absence of a wallet-to-buyer mapping in the captured files does not prove none exists elsewhere; only the three captured files were inspected
Analysis is confined to the three captured files; no CRM database, payment-processor backend, wallet mapping or CRM audit log was available.

The delegated source scope 'windows' is not registered in this task (platforms=[] and source_scopes=[]), so no Windows-derived evidence exists and the L2 Windows specialist mission (account usage, execution traces, persistence, device activity) could not be exercised.
The README is a case-description artifact, not independent forensic evidence; its linkage rules were corroborated against the actual field values in both data files.
Settlement lines carry only a date (2024-06-01 / 2024-06-02), not timestamps, so intra-day ordering and time-window correlation between CRM and settlement records is not possible.
Amount agreement (20000/15000/31500) supports the order_id join but is not itself a unique key; confirmation rests on the order_id string match.
warnings: ORD-72033 (settlement) and ORD-70233 (CRM) differ by a single digit transposition and are NOT the same order; equating them would misattribute a 9999 settlement to buyer sunli's 31500 order.
ORD-70234 is 'cancelled' in the CRM and has no settlement line; it must not be reported as a confirmed/paid order.
All three files share one capture timestamp (1790594136), so file-level timestamps cannot establish which source was modified first.
